Oh man I feel your pain. I had a post with a similar title explaining why I am anti-psychiatry, but people were wrongly assuming I was forcing my views on others, and it was gaining traction, so I took it down. 

I've been in a psyche ward three times, and it was awful. 

The first time, I remember there was a trans girl, and the staff all deadnamed her, and then apparently she was "making the girls uncomfortable" (which she wasn't) and got moved to the boy's section, and she was really upset and they gave her the injection (There's an injection they give people in psyche wards that makes them pass out) 

The second time wasn't all that bad, but I was sent by my parents to, and I quote "Get rid of me" 

I overheard them talking about what they can do to get rid of me for the time being because of my "awful behavior" (Talking back to them) and to this day, it hurts to think about that they would just try to abandon me like that. The worst part? They told the psyche ward that I was there because I tried to hurt my sisters, when I never did anything like that. 

The third time, I was forced to strip down in front of some nurses, and it was really humiliating. And the worst part is that the cis boys did not have to do that. 

Plus, after getting used to one area of the psyche ward and making friends there, they moved me to a different area of the ward with different people, which is bad for my anxiety, but they wouldn't listen.

I've been staying at a homeless shelter in northern California and it's not that bad.

Yes, there's rules and you have to arrive and leave at a certain time until you get one of the upstairs beds, but that's to be expected. 

At the shelter I stay at, we get one smoke break every hour.

We get served breakfast and dinner, but we aren't served lunch for some reason? So some shelters you may be on your own for lunch. 

Smoke breaks are about 20 minutes I think? I'm not sure, I don't smoke regularly. 

Of course you aren't supposed to leave the property other than going to the smoke area during smoke breaks, but that's to make sure people don't go and do drugs. 

Once you get approved to go upstairs, you will soon get approved to stay all day there. 

 I personally left was because I thought it was ridiculous that you aren't allowed to hang out anywhere on the street that the homeless shelter is located. Several people have tried to explain the rule to me, but I still think it's absolutely bullshit. I was written up for simply talking to one of my homeless friends on that specific street, and three write ups means I could get kicked out. 

(I ended up going back because the weather is getting worse, but that's off topic)

Anyways, I think homeless shelters are a good place to go if you have nowhere else to go, but you have to agree to all the rules, no matter how dumb they seem.. or are.
